description: Amid the collapse in private investment and stalled national projects, a group of EU member states with existing data centre infrastructure and energy surplus — notably Finland, Sweden, and Austria — quietly form a regional compute-sharing pact to pool remaining sovereign capacity. The arrangement is framed as emergency continuity, but includes binding commitments on mutual access, joint security audits, and shared maintenance of AI workloads for essential public services. This emergent coordination bypasses the stalled central compact and creates a de facto northern European compute bloc.
